inputs.root_cause: ORA-RESOLUTION-001 (2 obligations) had zero test-file mapping at all despite the resolution model, parser enforcement, and profile-0.0.3 detection logic already being fully built in document.py/stack_xml.py/lifecycle.py. ORA-ISOLATION-001 (2 obligations) had generic three-selector citations despite a dedicated 15-test file (test_obligation_isolation_semantics.py) already proving declared/inferred isolation and profile-0.0.4 detection; its own docstring explicitly scopes out actual pixel rendering as unbuilt.

execution_steps: 1. Surveyed ora's remaining capabilities by unresolved-obligation count. ORA-RESOLUTION-001 (2) and ORA-ISOLATION-001 (2) were the two smallest, both concerning lifecycle.py's _detect_version -- the profile-drift detector this session already relied on for XLIFF/UBL/NRRD's detected-vs-declared version work.

2. Read model/document.py (OraDocument.xres/yres, DEFAULT_RESOLUTION_PPI, __post_init__ positivity checks), codec/stack_xml.py's _resolution (specified-together enforcement, defaulting to 72 only when BOTH absent), and lifecycle.py's _detect_version/_uses_isolation (priority-ordered profile inference: isolation -> 0.0.4, non-default resolution -> 0.0.3, mergedimage-only -> 0.0.2, else 0.0.1).

3. Confirmed via existing tests (test_obligation_stack_and_document.py, test_obligation_document_model_construction.py) that pairing/positivity/defaulting were already fully proven at both parse time and direct-construction time. The one genuinely untested slice: a non-default resolution ALONE (no isolation used) is detected as profile 0.0.3, distinct from the 0.0.4 and 0.0.2 triggers -- every existing detected-version test either used isolation (triggering 0.0.4 first, since isolation is checked before resolution in _detect_version) or used no non-default resolution at all.

4. Wrote tests/python/ora/test_obligation_resolution_profile_detection.py (4 new tests): non-default resolution alone detects as 0.0.3; resolution outranks the mergedimage-only 0.0.2 trigger; declaring 0.0.3 with non-default resolution has no version drift; and a control proving default resolution (xres=yres=72, explicit but indistinguishable from absent) does NOT trigger 0.0.3. All 4 passed on first run.

5. Read test_obligation_isolation_semantics.py in full (15 tests, its own docstring already scoped to this exact obligation pair): declared isolation via the isolation attribute, inferred isolation via opacity<1 and non-default composite-op (each with its boundary control), declared-vs-inferred distinguishability, per-stack (non-inherited) evaluation, and profile-0.0.4 detection for both declared and inferred triggers. The docstring explicitly states 'render isolated groups against a transparent intermediate backdrop' is unbuilt (no rendering engine) and not claimed.
6. Ran all 15 isolation tests plus the 8 resolution parse-time tests plus the 5 resolution construction tests directly: all passed, unchanged.

7. Promoted SAL-ORA-OBL-0E1F1D54159FEFCC and SAL-ORA-OBL-FBBF45A773C7C0C9 (both ORA-RESOLUTION-001, neither obligation's rule_text mentions rendering) to implemented. Promoted SAL-ORA-OBL-97CE271E3DD6D883 (the compositing-TRIGGER rule -- isolation/opacity/composite-op conditions, no rendering language) to implemented. Left SAL-ORA-OBL-ABDDB437C86DC22F (the broader statement explicitly including 'render... against a transparent intermediate backdrop') at partial, narrowing missing_behavior to name exactly that unbuilt rendering clause -- the modeling and profile-enforcement halves it shares with its sibling are credited via updated source_symbols/tests, but the obligation as a whole is not force-closed.

evidence.oracle: none -- this is format_factory's own self-consistent test evidence, not independently verified against an external OpenRaster reader/writer. Labeled SELF-CONSISTENT per the FF6 execution-recovery directive's GAP-008 rule, not VERIFIED.
evidence.why_one_of_four_obligations_stayed_parti: SAL-ORA-OBL-ABDDB437C86DC22F's rule_text explicitly requires rendering isolated groups against a transparent backdrop -- actual pixel compositing this package has no rendering engine for. Forcing this to implemented would misrepresent an unbuilt capability; narrowed instead, matching this session's established GAP-008 discipline (NRRD kind-value enums, UBL/XLIFF tolerant-mode, XLIFF version-downgrade-loss were all declined on the same principle).
